title: Pear, Anjou, green, with skin, raw

content.title: About
content.content: Anjou pear is one of the most popular pear varieties, known for its fragrant aroma, sweet flavor, and crisp yet tender flesh. The green, skin‑on version retains all the nutrients of fresh pears and is typically enjoyed raw.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The Anjou cultivar originates from France and is named after the city of Angers.
Green Anjou pears ripen later than yellow ones and are prized in cooking for their firm texture.
The skin is rich in antioxidants, so it’s best left on.
Pears can be grown in temperate climates and are widely cultivated in the US, Europe, and Asia.
Pears do not continue to ripen fully after harvest, so they are usually picked when slightly soft.

items.title: High in fiber
items.content: Fiber supports digestion, promotes satiety, and helps regulate blood sugar levels.

items.title: Source of vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C boosts the immune system and aids collagen synthesis.

items.title: Contains potassium
items.content: Potassium helps maintain normal blood pressure and heart function.

items.title: Rich in antioxidants
items.content: Flavonoids and polyphenols in the skin protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Low‑calorie snack
items.content: Pears are low in calories, making them a good choice for weight management.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience an allergic reaction to pears.

items.title: Pesticide residues
items.content: As with many fruits, pears may carry pesticide residues; wash thoroughly before eating.

items.title: Digestive issues
items.content: Eating large amounts can cause gas and discomfort in people with sensitive stomachs.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Anjou pears can be eaten whole, sliced into salads, added to yogurt or oatmeal, or used in baking. Keeping the skin preserves the most nutrients.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store pears in the refrigerator’s fruit drawer, preferably in a paper bag to slow ripening. At room temperature they ripen quickly, so monitor their condition.
